solution.text: Due to the presence of six fluoride ligands and one lone pair of electrons in <math><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub></math> , the structure lacks perfect octahedral symmetry and is disordered. In <math><msup><mrow><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> all the valence shell electrons of xenon are involved in the bonding with oxygen and hence, no lone pair of electrons is present. So, it has perfect octahedral geometry.
